title: Compute Access Equity for Academic Researchers
bottleneck: Frontier AI research now requires compute at scales only a few companies possess, locking academic and public-interest researchers out of the experiments that matter. Public compute initiatives are orders of magnitude smaller than private training runs, creating a one-sided science of AI capabilities and safety. Safety research conducted without frontier access risks studying toy problems while real risks develop inside corporate labs.
why_it_blocks: If only industry can study frontier systems, independent safety science and public oversight become impossible. Democratic oversight of AI becomes hollow when only industry understands the systems.
current_state: The US NAIRR pilot and EU initiatives provide modest shared compute, far below frontier training scale. Public compute at even 1% of frontier scale would transform independent AI safety science.
